1.explanation:
• lib/emulation.js is where Lighthouse calls Page.setUserAgentOverride and injects the emulated mobile UA for network requests. If this override string isn’t propagated back into the LHR, the report will show a different UA.  
• gather/driver.js is responsible for communicating with the DevTools protocol and fetching the Browser.getVersion userAgent. That value is currently used to populate runtimeSettings.userAgent in the final report.  
• report/report-generator.js pulls the UA from Browser.getVersion (via driver) into LHR.runtimeSettings.userAgent. Because it never reads the emulation override, the printed UA doesn’t match what was actually sent.  
Fixing this requires reading the emulated override UA (from emulation.js) and feeding it into the runtimeSettings in report-generator.js (instead of—or in addition to—the Browser.getVersion value obtained in driver.js).
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse with a mobile emulation (e.g. emulated Nexus 5) Lighthouse sends one User-Agent header over the network (the mobile UA override) but records a different UA string in the report’s “Runtime settings → User agent” (the default Browser.getVersion UA). The mismatch is confusing because the UA you see in your webserver logs doesn’t match what Lighthouse prints.

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/lib/emulation.js is where the mobile emulation settings (including the UA override) are defined and pushed to the page via CDP’s Emulation.setUserAgentOverride.
• lighthouse-core/gather/driver.js implements the driver.getBrowserVersion() call that fetches the browser’s UA (used for runtimeSettings.userAgent) but does so _before_ or _instead of_ reading the emulated override.
• lighthouse-core/runner.js is where the LHR’s runtimeSettings.userAgent is populated from driver.getBrowserVersion(); it therefore surfaces the wrong UA string.  

To fix the mismatch, the code in runner.js (or in gather/driver.js) should use the same UA string that emulation.js has applied, rather than the raw Browser.getVersion UA.
2.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse runs in mobile emulation (for example, “Emulated Nexus 5X”) it installs a User-Agent override on the network via CDP (so your server logs show the emulated Android UA), but the string that Lighthouse prints under “Runtime settings → User agent” comes from Browser.getVersion (the desktop CrOS UA). The two values differ, which is confusing.
